title: Customer-specific long-tail generation for multi-token terminators after per-route sampling inheritance change
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Summary: A key enterprise customer has reported that evaluation runs (JSON-structured outputs) are seeing longer-than-expected tails and frequent extra sentences after the expected termination sequence. Regression was first observed after the per-route sampling inheritance change deployed to staging and later to a subset of Dedicated pools. The behaviour is customer-specific (same prompts produce different termination behavior only for their routed pool) and correlates with routes that have multi-token stop sequences and legacy per-route sampling overrides. This ticket drives triage, root cause analysis, and a safe hotfix + regression prevention for Hosted, Dedicated and Private environments.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use customer-provided prompt set (attached link) that expects a JSON body terminated by the token sequence '###
END' (three char sequence plus newline + 'END').

2) Send identical requests routed to the customer's dedicated pool and to a control hosted pool with identical model/version and global sampling defaults. Record outputs and token streams (streaming SSE logs).

3) Observe that dedicated pool runs produce additional trailing sentences ~12% of the time and frequently include a partial duplicate of the final JSON closing bracket, indicating termination was delayed by 6-18 tokens.

4) Re-run with explicit per-request sampling params (temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0) and with explicit stop token arrays set on the request. Confirm parity is restored for some runs but not consistently when the route config contains an override profile marked 'legacy-route-sampling: true'.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: change to per-route sampling inheritance (merged in runtime-1.21) altered precedence between route-level profiles and per-request sampling fields; some routes still have legacy profiles that leave sampling unspecified, causing runtime to fall back to a 'compat' sampler that behaves differently for stop-token matching when prefix/KV cache is hot.

Tokenization angle: customer uses mixed encodings and multi-token terminators (including a newline followed by 'END' and sometimes a zero-width non-joiner in localized prompts). We saw that the stop-detector runs a fast path requiring exact token-boundary alignment. If sampling allows low-prob tail tokens when KV cache contains a similar suffix, termination can be missed until an explicit soft-limit triggers.

Routing layer: header canonicalization recently stripped an internal 'x-rw-sample-level' header for routed requests in a fallback path, leading some Dedicated requests to be evaluated by the 'compat' sampler rather than the new deterministic sampler. Logs show 'sampler=compat-v1' for affected requests while control pool logs show 'sampler=deterministic-v2'.

Reproduction variance: We reproduced locally by simulating KV cache warm state and the legacy sampler; variance was non-deterministic but correlated strongly with KV cache hit ratio and sequence-length distribution.

Customer telemetry: Their eval harness reports higher BLEU/JSON-structure failures for samples that used the dedicated pool during a 72-hour window post-deploy. Most affected prompts contain multi-token terminators or trailing invisible characters.
root_cause: A change to per-route sampling inheritance changed precedence such that routes with legacy 'sampling_profile' unset were evaluated using a compatibility sampler. That sampler's stop-token matching fast-path does not correctly account for multi-token terminators when the KV cache contains a matching suffix, leading to delayed termination (long tail tokens). Additionally, the routing header canonicalization change caused some dedicated routes to lose the explicit sampler override header, widening the impact.
decision_log: Hotfix approach approved: restore explicit sampler precedence so per-request stop tokens and per-route explicit sampler overrides always win over compat fallback. This is a minimal patch to runtime sampler selection logic (priority fix in runtime-1.21-hotfix).

Short-term mitigation: push a config change to affected Dedicated pools to set 'sampling_profile: deterministic-v2' at the route level, and toggle stop-token normalization to 'strict' for the customer route until patch lands.

Long-term: add an automated parity test suite exercising multi-token terminators + KV cache warm states in CI and add a routing-layer contract test to ensure header preservation across fallthrough paths.
Notify customer with a technical write-up and offer to re-run their evals after hotfix; escalate to Solutions for coordinated verification and compensation if needed.
resolution_summary: Implemented patch to sampler precedence and deployed runtime-1.21-hotfix to staging, then to affected Dedicated pools. Config change applied to customer's route to pin 'deterministic-v2' sampler and strict stop normalization. Verified customer eval parity improved to baseline on 3/04/2025 across 5000 sample runs. Added regression tests and routing-layer header contract tests to CI. Customer notified and support engagement scheduled for post-deploy verification.
deploy_plan: 2) Deploy to staging and run full eval harness including KV-warm scenarios for determinism tests.
3) Roll out hotfix to a canary subset of Dedicated pools, monitor stop-token failure rate and tail token insertion metric (metric: eval.termination.delay > 2 tokens).
4) If metrics stable for 2 hours, roll out to remaining affected pools and push config pin for customer route.
rollback_plan: If termination regression worsens or other regressions detected: revert sampler-precedence change and configuration pin; restore previous runtime and re-open immediate investigation. Rollback steps documented in PR and on-call notified.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add parity test for multi-token terminators under KV-warm conditions to nightly CI.
2) Update routing header contract tests to assert sampler header preservation across all fallback codepaths.
3) Add metrics/traces for 'sampler' attribute at request-level to make affected requests searchable in Console.
4) Create a small runbook for Solutions/SEs outlining steps to apply per-route pins as a mitigation while fixes are pending.

2025-02-25 - Backend Review: Determined canonicalization change removed sampler header in one fallback path (PR #14877). This plus precedence reorder explains scope. Prioritizing hotfix patch to sampler selection.
